1.explanation:
1. gather/computed/critical-request-chains-test.js: Contains the unit tests for the computed artifact that builds the request-dependency graph and extracts critical request chains. Reviewing this shows how rel=preload is classified and measured.
2. audits/critical-request-chains-test.js: Verifies the audit logic (thresholds, scoring, headings) for reporting CR chains. Helps trace how the artifact feeds into the Audit and under what conditions it is flagged.
3. report/v2/renderer/crc-details-renderer-test.js: Tests the UI renderer for the CR-chains details in the generated report, including how links, timings, and waterfall views are assembled.
4. gather/computed/page-dependency-graph-test.js: The CR-chains artifact depends on the page dependency graph—this shows how resources (HTML → CSS) are linked and how rel=preload fits into the graph model.
5. audits/uses-rel-preload-test.js: Ensures that rel=preload usage is detected correctly. While this audit is separate, it shows how Lighthouse parses and treats rel=preload elements in the document, which may influence priority assignment.
6. gather/network-recorder-test.js: Illustrates how network activity (requests, timings) are captured. Understanding the raw records is necessary to see how the CSS request’s 5 s delay ends up in the CR chain artifact.
1.bug_scenario: The user’s test page (`preload-control.html`) uses a non-blocking CSS preload pattern: `<link rel="preload" as="style" href="slow.css.php" onload="this.rel='stylesheet';…">`. Even though this stylesheet never blocks rendering (and in the test contains no CSS), Lighthouse is still identifying it as part of a "critical request chain." The provided screenshot shows the Diagnostics panel under “Critical Request Chains,” listing two requests (the HTML and the slow CSS) with a total latency of ~5.9 s. The user wants to understand why Lighthouse treats a rel=preload resource as "critical," and what part of the CR-chain algorithm or audit logic triggers this warning.
